businessContext.companyDescription: Peerless Fence is a specialty contractor providing residential and commercial fence installation services. The company operates through Home Depot Service Center (HD) as a primary sales channel and uses ComputerEase (Deltek) for job costing and project management. Integration is required to automate lead-to-job workflows across HD Portal, Salesforce, and ComputerEase.
businessContext.budgetSignals: GCP infrastructure costs ~$5,000/month; Deltek support ticket submitted; no explicit budget envelope mentioned but cost optimization (cloud migration) discussed as future consideration

p0Flags.gotcha: ComputerEase/Deltek API requires CE Live Service relay; vendor support ticket mandatory; sandbox has no API access
p0Flags.clientAction: Do not attempt direct API calls to ComputerEase. All API requests must route through Deltek's CE Live Service relay. Sandbox environment cannot be used for API testing; production-only. Vendor support ticket already submitted; await response and follow Deltek's configuration guidance.
p0Flags.architectNote: CE Live Service is a legacy relay mechanism that intercepts API calls and routes them through Deltek's infrastructure to the on-premise GCP instance. This is not standard REST/SOAP; it requires special handling. Sandbox (P3) explicitly does not support API access.

p0Flags.gotcha: On-premise VM firewall rules allow SSH/RDP from anywhere (0.0.0.0/0); no source IP filtering; static IP exposed to internet
p0Flags.clientAction: Immediately restrict SSH (port 22) and RDP (port 445) ingress rules to known Peerless office IP ranges and VPN gateways only. Do not leave 0.0.0.0/0 open. Implement egress rules to prevent data exfiltration. Consider moving ComputerEase to Deltek's cloud-hosted version to eliminate on-premise infrastructure risk.
p0Flags.architectNote: Current firewall config: ingress allow-all on SSH/RDP; egress only enabled for 443/8081. ComputerEase listening on 445 (SMB/RDP), not 443. Static IP 35.222.218.224 is publicly routable. This is a critical security gap.

p0Flags.gotcha: Sandbox and production share single VM; no environment isolation; API configuration only in production
p0Flags.clientAction: Confirm with Deltek whether separate VMs can be provisioned for sandbox and production. If not, all API testing must occur in production with read-only (GET) operations only. Implement strict change control and rollback procedures. Consider Deltek cloud migration to enable proper environment separation.
p0Flags.architectNote: Single VM architecture means sandbox and production share the same ComputerEase instance, database, and firewall rules. API access is production-only. This violates standard integration best practices and increases risk of production incidents during testing.

p0Flags.gotcha: HD Portal login not yet provisioned; API credentials provided but portal access blocked; 10-minute sync lag between HD and Salesforce
p0Flags.clientAction: Follow up with Marius and HD support to provision portal login credentials for Datascape team. Verify API credentials are valid and test connectivity before proceeding. Plan for 10-minute data freshness lag in integration design; do not assume real-time sync.
p0Flags.architectNote: HD Portal login credentials not yet issued; API credentials provided but portal access failing ('user not recognized'). Lead sync from HD to Salesforce is asynchronous (10-minute intervals), not real-time. This affects job entry timing and data consistency validation.

p0Flags.gotcha: Quote line items contain unstructured product data with spelling errors and inconsistent naming; no data validation rules enforced at entry
p0Flags.clientAction: Create a data quality dashboard to flag quote line items with spelling errors, missing required fields (e.g., picket type for wood), or mismatched material types. Implement Salesforce validation rules to enforce material-type-dependent field requirements. Consider IDP (Intelligent Document Processing) to extract and validate data from scanned contracts.
p0Flags.architectNote: Sales reps manually enter product details (material type, picket type, post caps, gates) into quote line items. No validation enforces that wood materials require picket type, or that material names match a master list. Spelling errors ('pyramid' vs 'piramid') are common. This creates downstream data quality issues in ComputerEase job entry.

p0Flags.gotcha: Opportunity/Account data must match lead source; discrepancies block job entry; no automated reconciliation
p0Flags.clientAction: Implement a pre-job-entry validation flow in Salesforce that compares lead name, address, and contact info against Opportunity and Account records. Flag mismatches and require manual review before job entry to ComputerEase. Consider automating lead-to-opportunity conversion to reduce manual data entry errors.
p0Flags.architectNote: Lead data from HD Portal is manually verified against Salesforce Opportunity and Account records. Discrepancies (e.g., lead name 'Ashley Peerless' vs. contract name 'Muckian Test') are flagged as compliance issues and block job entry. No automated reconciliation exists.

p0Flags.gotcha: User permission model unclear; full admin access not automatically granted; separate maintenance account required for user creation
p0Flags.clientAction: Request Deltek support to clarify permission model and confirm that Datascape team has full admin access in sandbox. Verify that user creation, API configuration, and job entry permissions are all granted. Test each permission explicitly before proceeding with integration development.
p0Flags.architectNote: ComputerEase uses a legacy DOS-based permission model. Full admin access was claimed to be granted but not verified. User creation requires a separate 'PW_MAINTENANCE' account. Permission inheritance between sandbox and production is unclear.

p0Flags.gotcha: Business process includes manual document validation (contract compliance, signature legibility, date validation) with no automated rules engine
p0Flags.clientAction: Document all business rules for contract validation (e.g., 'permit date must be Friday', 'deposit amount must match contract total', 'signatures must be legible'). Create a rules engine or IDP workflow to automate validation. Flag exceptions for manual review by Ashley or designated approver.
p0Flags.architectNote: Contract validation is currently manual: Ashley reviews 299A and 299B documents, checks for legible signatures, verifies dates are Fridays, confirms deposit amounts match contract totals, and validates material types against quote line items. No automated rules engine exists. This is a bottleneck for scaling.

p0Flags.gotcha: Job entry requires manual mapping of budget worksheet data (material, labor, subcontractor, commission, overhead) to ComputerEase; no automated data flow
p0Flags.clientAction: Create a Salesforce flow or MuleSoft integration to automatically extract budget worksheet data and map it to ComputerEase job costing fields. Validate that all required fields are populated before posting to ComputerEase. Implement error handling and retry logic for failed submissions.
p0Flags.architectNote: Budget worksheet data (material cost $2,285.35, subcontractor $891.35, commission $582.25, overhead $671.15) is manually entered into ComputerEase job maintenance. No automated data flow exists. This is error-prone and time-consuming.

p0Flags.gotcha: ComputerEase VM infrastructure costs ~$5,000/month; Deltek cloud migration could reduce costs and improve reliability
p0Flags.clientAction: Request Deltek pricing for cloud-hosted ComputerEase. Compare total cost of ownership (infrastructure, support, security) against on-premise GCP hosting. Evaluate cloud migration as part of long-term roadmap to reduce operational overhead and improve environment isolation.
p0Flags.architectNote: Current GCP infrastructure costs approximately $5,000/month for a single beefy compute instance. Deltek offers cloud-hosted ComputerEase with modern API support and environment separation. Cloud migration could reduce costs and eliminate on-premise security/firewall management.
